subject: maths
title: Linear Graphs: y = mx + c
welcome_lead: Straight lines have a formula. Learn how m controls steepness and c sets where the line crosses.
meta_desc: Master y = mx + c, gradient and y-intercept in this KS3 graphs adventure.
final_note: Brilliant! Linear graphs are clear and easy now.

concepts.def: Straight-line graph in the form y = mx + c.
Steepness of a line, m in y = mx + c.
Where the line crosses the y-axis, c.
Rule linking x and y on the line.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In y = 2x + 3: m = 2 (gradient), c = 3 (y-intercept).

The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 3) and rises 2 for every 1 step right.

Make a table: x = 0 → y = 1, x = 1 → y = 2, x = 2 → y = 3.

Plot (0,1), (1,2), (2,3) and join with a ruler.

mcqs.q: In y = 4x + 7, what is the gradient?
In y = 3x - 2, where does the line cross the y-axis?
What does the gradient of a straight-line graph tell you?
options: How steep the line is — the change in y for each unit change in x (rise over run).
The x value where the line crosses the x-axis.
Where the line crosses the y-axis.
How long the line is on the page.

mcqs.q: In the equation y = 3x + 5, what does the 5 represent on the graph?
options: The x value where the line crosses the x-axis.
How long the line is on the page.
The y-intercept — the value of y when x = 0 (where the line crosses the y-axis).
The gradient — how steep the line is.

mcqs.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal line mean?
options: How long the line is on the page.
The object is moving backwards.
The object is moving at a constant speed.
The object is stationary — distance is not changing, so speed is zero.
